From the owner
Central Florida voted — and KBF Design Gallery was named a 2026 Central Florida Favorite three times over. 🥇 Gold — Remodeler / Contractor 🥇 Gold — Kitchen & Bath Remodeler 🥈 Silver — Interior Design Firm Central Florida Favorites is the Orlando Sentinel's annual community-choice program: readers across the region nominate and vote for the local businesses they trust most. No panel, no paid application. Winners were announced in the Winner's Magazine inserted in the Sunday, July 26 Orlando Sentinel. Two Gold awards recognize the heart of our work — full-scale kitchen and bath remodels and whole-home renovations delivered by one accountable design-build team. The Silver in Interior Design reflects a practice that has grown right alongside it. To our clients across Orlando, Winter Park, Windermere, Baldwin Park, Lake Mary, and Maitland who trusted us with their homes and then took a moment to vote: thank you. Considering a kitchen, bathroom, or whole-home project? Visit our Maitland showroom or read the full story.
Jul 28, 2026

THE CASE STUDIES — NINE DEEP DIVES

Full-scope studies of our biggest transformations — the design decisions, the structure we found, and the rooms that came out of it.

CASE STUDY
CS 01 — WINDERMERE — CASE STUDY
The California Modern Estate
A Windermere whole-home remodel that changed everything but the walls — travertine to white oak, the rebuilt kitchen, the great room, the wine room. See the judgment.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 02 — WINTER GARDEN — CASE STUDY
The Lakefront Great Room
Case study: a Winter Garden lakefront home's social floor rebuilt as one entertaining room — a two-island kitchen, custom fireplace built-ins, and a true bar, with real before-and-after photos and the materials named from the project's order records.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 03 — APOPKA — CASE STUDY
The Two-Tone Transitional
Case study: a 2014 Apopka builder-spec home remade as one airy black-and-white main floor — a two-tone kitchen, continuous hickory floors, an engineered French-door opening cut into the concrete-block wall, and a rebuilt primary bath, with real before-and-after photos and the materials named from the project's order records.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 04 — CELEBRATION — CASE STUDY
The Organic Modern
A Celebration home remodeled in phases by KBF's design-build team — sage-and-oak kitchen under a slatted ceiling, gathering rooms in rattan and black, and a stone-and-oak primary bath. Real photos, real walkthrough film.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 05 — WINTER PARK — CASE STUDY
The Ivory Classic
A Winter Park home replanned around one kitchen decision — the range moved, the machines hidden in cabinetry — then finished in two phases through a veined-stone primary bath. Real photos, the real one-minute walkthrough.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 06 — WINDERMERE — CASE STUDY
The Lantern Classic
A 2006 Mediterranean Windermere home remodeled from its own permitted plan set — new arches framed, a hutch in a purpose-built recess, a curved stainless hood, and a rebuilt pool bath. With the real before-and-after of the same wall.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 07 — WINTER PARK — CASE STUDY
The White Oak Ranch
A midcentury Winter Park ranch taken decades forward — white-oak cabinetry and brass throughout, the wall between the family and living rooms opened, and a bedroom traded for the primary suite. With drag-to-reveal before-and-afters, including the same street corner.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 10 — CLERMONT — CASE STUDY
The Lakeside Blue
A Clermont lakefront home opened up — the wall between the kitchen and family room removed for an expansive island, a primary bath squared off around a zero-entry shower, a new stacked stone fireplace wall, and one floor running through the house. Real before-and-after photos and the real walkthrough film.
READ THE STUDY →
CASE STUDY
CS 11 — OCOEE — CASE STUDY
The Same Street, New Story
An Ocoee home on a street its owners loved, rebuilt from the slab up — the ceiling raised, a second story added, and a lanai, outdoor kitchen and pool across the back. Real before-and-after photos and the real walkthrough film.
READ THE STUDY →

SEE THE RECORDS

WALK IT BY SERVICE

Kitchen remodeling is the deepest shelf on the wall — full-gut transformations from modern farmhouse in Mount Dora to the waterfall-island moderns of Maitland's Dommerich Estates. Every kitchen here was designed, built, and finished by one KBF team, cabinetry through appliances.

Bathroom remodeling runs from a mid-century master bath to an accessible luxury wet room — including the steam-shower bath that remains one of the most-visited projects we've ever published.

Whole-home remodeling is where the featured transformations live: Winter Park, Windermere, Mount Dora, Celebration, Maitland, Apopka — entire homes rethought room by room under one contract, one team, one schedule.

And the spaces between: additions, outdoor living, wine rooms, speakeasy parlors, and the interior-design practice that furnishes and finishes what the construction team builds.

CASE STUDIES

The whole story behind a finished room.

A gallery shows you the after. A case study shows you the judgment — the wall that had to be opened, the beam that carried it, the sequence that kept a family in their home. These are real KBF projects, told from the drawing to the last drawer pull.

THE STUDIES

OCOEE — WHOLE-HOME REBUILD, SECOND STORY, LANAI & POOL

The Same Street, New Story

Homeowners who loved their neighborhood and needed a house that fit — rebuilt from the slab up with a raised ceiling, a second story, and a lanai, outdoor kitchen and pool across the back. With the real before-and-afters and the completion walkthrough film.

READ THE CASE STUDY

CLERMONT — KITCHEN, PRIMARY BATH, FIREPLACE & FLOORING

The Lakeside Blue

A lakefront home bought for its view, then opened up to match it — the wall between the kitchen and the family room removed for an expansive island, a primary bath squared off around a zero-entry shower, a full-height stacked stone fireplace wall, and one floor carried through the house. With the real before-and-afters and the completion walkthrough film.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINTER PARK — WHOLE-HOME, COMPREHENSIVE

The White Oak Ranch

A midcentury ranch remodeled comprehensively in one pass — new systems beneath, the dark U kitchen opened into a white-oak island room, and a primary bath built where a bedroom used to be. With drag-to-reveal before-and-afters from the family’s own camera corners, and the real 44-second walkthrough film.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINTER PARK — WHOLE-HOME, IN TWO PHASES

The Ivory Classic

A Winter Park home replanned from one consultation into two phases — a cream-and-walnut kitchen with the range moved to the long wall, new white-oak floors, an entertainment wall, and a marble-wrapped primary bath. With the real one-minute walkthrough film.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINDERMERE — WHOLE-HOME REMODEL

The California Modern Estate

A dated Windermere estate traded travertine and heavy finishes for white oak, warm brass, and rooms that open to the oaks — a whole-home transformation that never needed to move a structural wall. See the finished home, and the judgment underneath it.

READ THE CASE STUDY

CELEBRATION — WHOLE-HOME, IN PHASES

The Organic Modern

A Celebration home remodeled in phases by the same team, one calm palette throughout — sage and white oak in the kitchen, rattan and black metal in the gathering rooms, stone and oak-look plank in the primary bath. With the real 49-second walkthrough film.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINDERMERE — KITCHEN, ENTERTAINMENT WALL & POOL BATH

The Lantern Classic

A 2006 Mediterranean home whose remodel built its own arches — a navy island under brass lanterns, a glass-front hutch in a purpose-built arched recess, a curved stainless hood, and a rebuilt pool bath, quoted from the project’s own permitted plan set. With the real before-and-after of the same wall.

READ THE CASE STUDY

APOPKA — KITCHEN, LIVING & PRIMARY SUITE

The Two-Tone Transitional

A 2014 builder-spec home became one airy black-and-white main floor — and the “simple” door swap turned out to be an engineered opening cut into a concrete-block wall. See the rooms, and the X-Ray of the frame that carries them.

READ THE CASE STUDY

REUNION — KITCHEN & PRIMARY BATH

The Corner That Stayed

The consult sheet flagged a load-bearing column that had to stay — so KBF opened the kitchen around it and built a 120-inch wine rack into it. With an X-ray view of what was removed and what still carries the house, and the builder bath reborn as a black-tile wet room.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINTER SPRINGS — PRIMARY BATH & STEAM SHOWER

The Steam Shower, Done Right

A primary bath planned for steam before a single tile went up — the concealed generator and its access, overhead supply lines, a honed-hex ceiling built to grip, and real steam photographed on the finished shower. Wipe the fogged glass to see what the steam hides.

READ THE CASE STUDY

WINTER GARDEN — KITCHEN, FIREPLACE & BAR

The Lakefront Great Room

A lakefront home’s social floor — kitchen, fireplace wall, and bar — rebuilt as one bright entertaining room, with real before-and-after photography and the materials named from the project’s own order records.

READ THE CASE STUDY

SHOWCASE — THE AWARD-WINNING ROOMS

The Winners

First place in 2022, 2024, 2025 and 2026 — and never below Merit since 2021. The winning rooms themselves, at full scale — the New Orleans inspired bar, the DeLand kitchen, the bespoke wine bar — each award stamped beside the work on one bronze rail of years.

SEE THE WINNING ROOMS

More case studies are being added as their photography and stories are documented. In the meantime, browse the full body of work or the county-verified record of resales.

COUNTY-VERIFIED · ORANGE / SEMINOLE / LAKE DEEDS · AS OF JUNE 2026

The Record: What the Central Florida Homes We Remodeled Sold For — Verified Against County Deeds

Most homes we remodel never sell — the owners stay. Of the ones that did sell, and that we could check against public county deed records, 9 of 13 finished among the top three prices ever recorded on their street or in their community — 7 of them at #1.

13
HOMES TRACKED THROUGH RESALE
9
FINISHED TOP-3 ON THEIR STREET OR COMMUNITY
7
OUTRIGHT #1 — A RECORD AT TIME OF SALE

We don't claim our remodel caused it. We show what the market did.

BOOK YOUR COMPLIMENTARY CONSULTATION407-499-8694

BEFORE YOU READ THE WALL

Why only thirteen homes? Because KBF clients overwhelmingly stay. A remodel here is built for the family living in it, not for a listing photo — so the set of homes that ever came back to market is small. We tracked every resale we could verify against public county deed records, and only those. No portal estimates, no self-reported numbers.

And we publish the ones that didn't set a record, too — they're in the full ledger below. That's the difference between a record and a highlight reel.

The 13 homes below are part of a body of work that spans 1,000+ projects across Central Florida (derived from 22 years of project records — verified). The wall isn't a promise about your home. It's evidence of how the market has treated this one builder's work, on the public record, where anyone can check it.

HOW WE VERIFIED IT

Every figure on this page comes from recorded deeds at the Orange County, Seminole County, and Lake County property appraisers — not from listing portals or estimates. Rankings compare a home's sale price against every prior sale recorded on the same street (or, where stated, in the same named community — or, for condominiums, in the same building), as of the sale date.

Junk records were excluded before ranking: bulk plat placeholders, nominal hundred-dollar transfers, and multi-parcel deeds. Each plate states its exact basis — street or community, price or price-per-square-foot — and the date it was true. Verify any of it yourself at the county parcel search; we cite the source and the recorded date on every row.

WHAT THIS PAGE IS NOT

Past performance is not a promise. We make no claim that a KBF remodel caused these outcomes, and no claim about what any future home will sell for — correlation is not causation. Every figure is dated and sourced to public county deed records as of its sale date; records reflect the market at the time of sale, not a guaranteed future result. Most KBF clients never sell at all — which is its own kind of record.

FROM THE KBF PROJECT REEL · shown for atmosphere — not one of the 13 tracked records.

THE REST OF THE EVIDENCE

On this page the pairing is record × deed citation, by design — we don't pin a named review to a sold address, because a seller's privacy outlasts our marketing. The named reviews live with their own projects: 4.8★ on Google across 63 reviews, each one real and matchable.

THE WINNERS

The rooms the judges couldn’t look away from.

First place in 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026, a national Silver in Qualified Remodeler’s 2026 Master Design Awards — and never below Merit since 2021. The Anatomy of a Remodel

Every element you can see, and every layer you can’t, is a decision someone had to get right. Explore 189 of them in one Windermere primary bath.

Isleworth · Windermere · from the KBF project record · consultation January 2021

0 of 189 decisions explored

WHY THIS PAGE EXISTS

A finished room is a hundred decisions standing quietly.

The room above is real: a complete-gut primary bath in Isleworth, Windermere, from KBF’s project records. The clients’ brief, quoted from the consultation record: “Complete gut … Linen storage. Better closet storage. Keep a tub. Separate vanities.” Between that sentence and the finished photograph sit 189 decisions: the questions below are the ones our designers and project managers actually answer, in the order the build forces them. Nothing here is theoretical.

Complete gut

One team
design through final walkthrough

The same beneath-the-finishes discipline runs wall-by-wall through The Two-Tone Transitional, our X-Ray flagship case study.

THE WET ROOM

The most decision-dense hundred square feet in the house.

The shower stack alone holds 20 decisions. Open it in the room above, or read every one below.

FLORIDA DESIGN SEAGLASS · FIRST PLACE · 2025
The judges read this room the same way. At the 2025 Florida Design Seaglass Awards, this Windermere spa retreat was named best traditional/transitional primary bathroom. The award hangs in The Winners.

04 / 11
Countertops and Surfaces

DOMAINS

THE WRITTEN TAXONOMY

All 189 decisions, in eleven domains.
THE ROOM IN QUESTION
Every decision below was made about this one room — a complete-gut primary bath in Isleworth, Windermere. Eleven domains, 189 calls, one photograph.

This is the same material our team carries into every project, written out in full: the question, what it depends on, the expert call, and what it costs to skip. Cross-referenced decisions appear once under their owning domain; where construction code governs a decision, the posture is confirmed at permit, never guessed.

FIND A DECISION

All 189 decisions, in eleven domains. Type a word and the list narrows to it.

CONTENTS
every decision by name · 189
DOMAIN 02 · TILE
Three of the decisions above meet on this one line: where the mosaic stops, how the marble curb is mitred, and where the glass lands on it. They are made weeks apart and read together, from standing height, forever.
04

DOMAIN 04 ·
19 DECISIONS

Countertops and Surfaces

The countertop is the single most-touched, most-stared-at surface in the whole remodel. It's also the last major thing fabricated and the first thing a guest lays a hand on. Every decision below gets locked before a saw ever touches a slab — and once it's cut, it's cut. This is where a hundred small expert calls hide inside one seamless-looking stone.

Countertop material — matching the stone to how they actually live
Bath surface material — the cosmetics-and-standing-water calculus
Slab thickness — 2cm vs 3cm and where each belongs
Edge buildup — mitering a thick edge onto a thin slab
Edge profile — the eased/beveled/ogee decision
Surface finish — polished vs honed vs leathered
Working-edge overhang — the standard countertop projection
Seating overhang — the stone-thickness cantilever nuance
Seam placement — hiding the joint where the eye won't travel
Vein-matched seams — making the movement cross the joint
Slab selection and book-matching — which half of the slab goes where
Vein continuation up the full-height backsplash — the waterfall of the wall
Backsplash height — 4-inch vs full-height vs none
Backsplash returns and terminations — how the splash dies at a window, wall, or open end
Waterfall ends — the mitered, vein-wrapped panel to the floor
Undermount sink reveal — positive, negative, or flush
Sink support and rodding — holding a heavy sink under stone
Faucet and deck-accessory hole layout — the drilled-hole committee
Cutout corner radii and fabrication tolerance — why a square inside corner cracks
Substrate and cabinet leveling before template — the flatness everything rides on
← CABINETRY
ALL ELEVEN DOMAINS
LIGHTING →
DOMAIN 4 OF 11
DOMAIN 04 · COUNTERTOPS AND SURFACES
Edge profile, overhang, undermount reveal, where the seam falls, how far the faucet reaches over the basin. The counter carries a stack of the decisions above at once, and every one of them is read from eighteen inches away.
05

DOMAIN 05 ·
19 DECISIONS

Lighting

Lighting is the layer people notice last and feel first. Get it right and the room reads calm, expensive, and effortless — the counters glow, faces look good in the mirror, and nothing hums or flickers. Get it wrong and it's the one thing you can't un-see: shadows on the cutting board, a blue light next to a warm one, a chandelier that looks like a earring on a linebacker. Here is nearly every decision that hides inside "we did the lighting."

Whole-Room Plan — Design three light layers, not one
Ambient Fill — Space the downlights to the ceiling, not by eye
Counter & Work Downlights — Aim at the work, not the room
Recessed Trim — Choose aperture size and trim color
Under-Cabinet Task Light — Hide it at the front edge
Island Pendants — Size and count to the island
Island Pendants — Set the hanging height
Glass-Cabinet & Interior Lighting — Light the display
Toe-Kick & Night Lighting — The low glow layer
Backsplash & Accent Aiming — Graze the texture
Vanity Lighting — Cross-light the face, not the top of the head
Mirror Sconces — Place them off the mirror's edges
Backlit Mirror vs. Sconces — Choose the vanity strategy
Shower & Wet-Location Fixtures — Rate for the zone
Fixture Over the Tub — Scale and safe height
Color Temperature — Lock every fixture to one Kelvin
Color Rendering (CRI) — Choose how true colors read
Dimming — Match dimmers to the LED drivers, zone by layer
Switch Layout — Zone the controls at the door
← COUNTERTOPS AND SURFACES
ALL ELEVEN DOMAINS
PLUMBING FIXTURES AND ROUGH-IN →
DOMAIN 5 OF 11
DOMAIN 06 · PLUMBING FIXTURES AND ROUGH-IN
The head and the two trims are the only part of this a client ever sees. Their heights, their spacing and the wall behind them were fixed months earlier, at rough-in, before a single tile went up.
DOMAIN 08 · WALLS, STRUCTURE, EXISTING CONDITIONS
A niche is a hole cut in a wall that was already carrying something. Its depth is decided by what is in the cavity — framing, a vent run, a valve body — not by the shelf anyone wanted.
DOMAIN 10 · SPACE PLANNING AND FLOW
The opening decides the room. Where this arch lands sets the sightline from the bedroom, the swing of everything behind it, and whether the tub reads as the centre of the room or as an object standing in it.
189 decisions. One team accountable for all of them.

You are not supposed to carry this list. That is what the fixed-fee design phase is for: every one of these questions, answered in sequence, before the first hammer swings.

A wall that carries joists, a wall under a second-floor wall, and a wall near the middle of the span are all treated as bearing until proven otherwise, and in Central Florida block homes the exterior walls are the real workhorses."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "How large can the floor tile be before the flatness of THIS subfloor stops cooperating, and does the room read better with a big calm field or a smaller module?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "large-format floor tile (commonly 12\"\u00d724\", 24\"\u00d724\", or larger) gives a luxury, low-grout, expansive read \u2014 but large format is unforgiving, so the substrate has to be flat within roughly 1/8\" over 10 feet, which usually means a self-leveling or mud-bed correction first. Big tile is a substrate-prep decision disguised as an aesthetic one."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "How big is the shower, does it go curbless, and does it even need a door \u2014 or is it a walk-in with a splash panel?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A comfortable single shower wants a ~36\"\u00d748\" interior; a luxe walk-in with a bench and two heads wants 42\"\u00d760\" or more. Curbless is the premium move, but it has to be decided now \u2014 it requires dropping or building up the floor structure to slope the pan to the drain, which is nearly impossible to add later. A walk-in past about 4 ft of clear opening, with the head aimed inward, often skips the door entirely. Minimum sizes and the waterproofing and slope details are governed by current Florida residential code and confirmed at permit."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Double vanity or single with a makeup drop-zone, what finished height, drawer banks or door cabinets \u2014 and where does the plumbing wall force the drawers to notch around the P-trap?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Modern primary-bath vanities run taller than the old 32\" standard \u2014 \"comfort height\" around 34.5\"\u201336\" so nobody stoops to brush their teeth (unless there's a seated makeup section, which drops to about 30\"). Drawers beat doors for real toiletry storage, but the sink's drain runs right through the drawer path, so those drawers get U-notched around the P-trap \u2014 a detail that has to be drawn before the box is built. A double vanity centers each sink in its zone with drawer banks stacked between, not a symmetrical afterthought."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Can we hang a statement chandelier over the freestanding tub, and if so how high must its bottom sit above the tub rim \u2014 and is the ceiling framed to hold it?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A chandelier over a soaking tub is a defining luxury-bath move \u2014 and its safe minimum height above the tub and its rim is governed by current Florida residential code \u2014 confirmed at permit, because the concern is a wet person reaching a fixture. Beyond the code height, the fixture must be damp-rated for the humid zone and, if it's heavy, the ceiling needs blocking or a rated brace box installed during framing to carry the weight and any sway. We size it to hang as a jewel above the tub without dominating the room, and we lock the location before the ceiling closes."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Which wall and which stud bay can actually hold a niche \u2014 because it has to fit between the studs, at a height that's useful, and I will not carve it into an exterior wall or a wall full of pipe if I can help it?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A niche wants to live in the cavity between two studs \u2014 roughly 14.5 inches of clear width at standard 16-inch-on-center framing \u2014 so a standard niche is that width unless we cut a stud and header it to go wider, which is more work and structural coordination. We center it around 48\u201352 inches up, at eye-and-reach level for the standing user, and keep it off exterior walls when there's an interior option, because an exterior-wall niche means carving into insulation and inviting condensation. And we confirm what's behind that bay first \u2014 you do not discover the vent stack after you've cut the hole."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Which primary-bath comforts \u2014 heated floor, warming towel bar, mirror defogger \u2014 are going in, and have their circuits, thermostats, and controls been decided before the tile and walls close, since every bit of it gets buried?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "A heated floor runs on its own thermostat circuit, with the sensor and mat laid under the tile \u2014 there is no adding it later without tearing out the floor. A hardwired towel warmer wants a timer so it isn't cooking all day, and a mirror defogger is wired behind the glass. Every one of these is a pre-tile, pre-close decision; the loads also get checked against panel headroom."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Cabinet white, quartz white, subway-tile white, farmhouse-sink white, trim white, and the plumbing fixture's 'white' \u2014 are these all the same white, or six different whites pretending to match?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "There is no such thing as \"just white\" \u2014 every white product carries an undertone (blue, gray, green, yellow, pink), and a luxury room is where they either all agree or intentionally step. We physically assemble every white in the room side by side on one board and cull the outliers. Plumbing is the sneaky one: a \"white\" toilet or tub is often biscuit/almond and will read dingy next to a true-white cabinet. Either we align them all to one undertone family or we set a clear value step (bright white trim, soft white cabinet) so the difference reads as intentional, not as a mistake."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Before we hang and close these walls, is every in-wall decision actually locked \u2014 plumbing rough-in locations, blocking, niche and bench framing, the waterproofing approach, low-voltage and lighting boxes, the exact fixtures that dictate rough heights?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Drywall is a one-way door. The moment it closes, every in-wall decision is either right or it's a demolition. So there's a hard gate before drywall: walk the open walls against the final selections and confirm the pot-filler is roughed to the actual range height, the shower valve is set to the chosen head, the niche is framed, the blocking is in for everything heavy or future, the vanity supply lines match the selected vanity, and the waterproofing plan is settled. Half the regrets in this whole section trace back to one selection that wasn't final when the walls closed. The captain's job is to force those decisions before the gate, not after."}}]}]}

THE DESIGN-BUILD DIFFERENCE

Custom kitchen design, remodeling & renovation —
one team
 

KBF Design Gallery is a design-build kitchen remodeler serving Orlando and Central Florida — custom kitchen design, remodeling, and full renovation under one team. Here, kitchen remodeling is a fully integrated design-to-build experience, tailored to how you live, cook, gather, and entertain. Our team of award-winning designers and experienced builders collaborates closely with you to create a kitchen that balances beauty, functionality, and long-term value.

From space planning and material selection to custom cabinetry and finishing details, every decision is guided by thoughtful design, craftsmanship, and a deep understanding of how a kitchen should perform every day. From single-room refreshes to full home additions and new-build interiors, KBF handles every phase of a Central Florida home project.

Whether your vision is modern, transitional, or timelessly classic, we specialize in creating custom kitchens that feel effortless yet intentional. Seamless layouts, smart storage solutions, and carefully curated finishes come together to transform your kitchen into the true heart of your home.

With KBF Design Gallery, you gain a trusted partner who manages every phase of the process, delivering a kitchen that is as refined as it is functional — and designed to stand the test of time.

WHY THE KITCHEN

The heart of the home

THERE'S A REASON the kitchen is often said to be the heart of the home: it’s where family and friends ultimately gather to enjoy a bite to eat and good company. However, the kitchens of today are much more than simply a place to cook and eat. Modern kitchens also function as dining rooms, offices and classrooms - they are truly the "hubs" of the home. If your kitchen is doing double or even triple-duty, it's essential that the space is maximized to function for you. We can help turn your kitchen into not only the perfect space for you to prepare meals, but a sanctuary that fulfills the needs of your entire family.

Many people are unsure about where to start with their kitchen remodel, and we know that taking the first step can be daunting. The home remodeling experts at KBF can help bring your kitchen renovation dream to life.

From concept to completion, KBF Design Gallery can reconfigure your current space and design the kitchen of your dreams. Our design team will focus on the features and functions that are important to you to ensure your new kitchen works for your lifestyle. We can introduce you to some of the latest kitchen design innovations and features to maximize your investment.

WE BEGIN BY ASKING QUESTIONS to learn all we can about your remodeling goals. We want to know what's prompting you to remodel your kitchen, what you like and don't like about your current kitchen, what you like about kitchens you may be inspired by (share the pictures with us!), and how you want your kitchen to work for you. We also want to know what you are looking for in a design and remodeling firm, because we know it's imperative, right from the beginning, that we are a good fit for you and your project. We strongly believe that the designer/client relationship is of the utmost importance to ensure the ideal outcome.

Over the past 20-plus years, KBF Design Gallery has earned the reputation as a trusted kitchen, bath and home design-to-build firm in Orlando and the surrounding areas. We believe this is because our approach to every project is the same: we listen to you so we can design for your individual needs, wants, style and investment.

WHILE THE KITCHEN IS OPEN

The remodel that starts in the kitchen
rarely ends there

ONCE THE KITCHEN IS OPEN, the house starts talking. The wall between the kitchen and the great room — usually load-bearing — is the difference between a nicer kitchen and a transformed first floor; where it carries weight, we engineer the move honestly (an LVL beam with engineered posts, sized and permitted, never guessed). The butler’s pantry, the laundry room off the kitchen, the flooring that should run continuous through the living spaces — these cost less to do while the walls are already open than they ever will again. In Clermont, that conversation opened a kitchen that had been closed off from the family room: the wall came out, an expansive island took its place, and the new flooring ran through the house while it was open — The Lakeside Blue.

That is a planning conversation, not an upsell: we scope what the house wants, you decide what the moment justifies. When the answer grows past the kitchen, our whole-home design-build team is the same team — and when the right move is refresh-in-place with the layout you have, Studio KBF exists for exactly that.

WHAT GOES INTO A KBF KITCHEN

Materials we put our name behind

Every KBF kitchen is specified transparently: premium custom and semi-custom cabinet lines built for Florida humidity, natural stone and engineered quartz from fabricators we have worked with for years, and appliance packages your family will actually use — selected together in our Maitland showroom so you see the exact door style, the exact slab, the exact hardware in real light before anything is ordered.

YOU SEE THE ALLOWANCES and the selections in writing, at trade pricing passed through — what we pay is what you see. No mystery brands, no bait-and-switch substitutions mid-project: any change to a specified material is documented and approved by you before it happens. Ask us in the showroom and we will happily name every manufacturer in your kitchen, and why we chose them.

Custom Bathroom Remodeling in Orlando

Design, build and finish — one team, one roof. Luxury bathroom renovations and remodels from Winter Park to Windermere, by KBF Design Gallery.

DESIGN-BUILD · ONE ROOF

One team from the first sketch
to the final grout line

Most bathroom projects in Central Florida are stitched together: a designer here, a general contractor there, a tile sub nobody has met yet.
Every hand-off is a place where the design intent — and the budget — leaks.
KBF Design Gallery is a design-build remodeling firm: the people who design your bathroom renovation are the same team that builds it, orders for it, and stands behind it.

IT STARTS in our Maitland showroom, where cabinetry, stone, tile, plumbing fixtures and lighting live under one roof, so selections happen in days instead of months. IT CONTINUES through a six-phase process with a dedicated project manager, written scope, and a schedule your family can actually plan around. AND IT ENDS with a bathroom remodel that looks like the drawings — because the drawings and the crew came from the same place.

That single-team promise is why homeowners searching for a bathroom contractor keep landing on remodels we finished a decade ago that still look current.
We are not the cheapest bid in Orlando.
We are the one that shows up with a designer, an engineer's respect for your house, and a five-year craftsmanship warranty.

IT ALSO CHANGES what a bid means. A one-trade bathroom remodeler prices the tile they can see; a design-build team scopes the whole room — what the demo will reveal, where the water lines actually run, whether that vanity wall can take the sconces you want. Our written estimates are fixed-scope: the number you approve is tied to drawings and selections you've already made, and any change afterward is documented and approved in writing before it touches cost or schedule. Renovation without that discipline is how Central Florida homeowners end up in the horror stories; remodeling with it is why our clients come back for the kitchen, the addition, and the next house.

WHY IT MATTERS

One contract, one accountable team — no designer-vs-contractor finger-pointing.
Showroom selections under one roof — see the stone, the tile and the hardware together, in real light.
Licensed & insured — Florida Certified General Contractor CGC 1529022.
We can move the wall — in-house structural capability most bath remodelers simply don't have.
Five-year craftsmanship warranty — in writing, honored.

BEFORE & AFTER · WINTER PARK

The window never moved.
The bath around it did.

One Winter Park primary bath, photographed toward the same shuttered window. A tiled-deck garden tub became a freestanding soaker beside a frameless walk-in shower with basketweave mosaic — the plantation shutters hold the frame. Drag the line.

THE WORK
AS FOUND

WINTER PARK · FROM THE WHOLE-HOME REMODEL IN THE IVORY CLASSIC

SCOPE

What a KBF custom bathroom includes

“Custom” is not a finish level — it is a way of designing from your routines outward. Some clients come to us for a primary suite that finally feels like the hotels they travel for; some need a hall bath that survives three kids; some are planning to age in place with zero compromise on beauty. A KBF custom bathroom design begins with how you live, then bends layout, storage, light and water around it.

EVERY PROJECT GETS full working drawings, real waterproofing detail (not caulk-and-hope), and finish carpentry held to furniture standards. Whether it is a renovation of a 1990s builder bath or a full gut remodel with the walls moving, the scope below is all in-house.

Keeping your layout? See Studio KBF — same-footprint remodels: the streamlined, designer-curated path for a bath transformed without moving walls. The page you are reading is our full-custom Signature bath practice.

The current wave of Central Florida bathroom design leans spa-like — wet rooms that turn the whole floor into the shower, steam enclosures, honed stone in place of gloss, layered warm lighting instead of one hostile ceiling fixture. We build all of it, but we design it to your house: a spa bath in a Baldwin Park townhome and one in a Windermere estate solve different problems with the same calm. What they share is what's behind the tile — waterproofing, slope, ventilation and structure detailed like the finish depends on it, because it does.

Primary & master suites — full-suite remodels, closets and dressing areas included.
Spa-like & wet-room showers — full-room waterproofing, linear drains, bench and niche work.
Curbless & steam showers — flush thresholds, vapor-sealed enclosures, the structure done right.
Freestanding tubs — floor-set plumbing, reinforced framing where the slab demands it.
Double vanities & vanity towers — custom cabinetry with real storage engineering.
Powder rooms — small rooms, outsized design.
Aging-in-place & accessible baths — grab-bar blocking, curbless entries, lighting for older eyes — designed beautifully, never clinically.

SELECTED BATHROOMS · CENTRAL FLORIDA

This is the reviewer’s actual master bath in Apopka, photographed at completion — their home, not a staging crew.

THE KBF DIFFERENCE

Zero-entry showers, wet rooms and steam

The strongest current in Central Florida bathroom design is the spa bath that works for every decade of your life: a curbless shower you simply walk into — no curb, no step, no threshold — a wet room that turns the entire floor into one waterproofed vessel, and a steam enclosure that ends the day somewhere better than it started. We design and build all three in-house, and the beauty is engineered: a flush entry means the floor is rebuilt to fall toward its drain, and a steam shower is only as good as its vapor seal, its slope and its ventilation.
What’s behind the tile is the luxury.

Zero-entry is also the quietly brilliant aging-in-place decision — the same threshold-free room that photographs like a resort serves you without compromise decades from now. Grab-bar blocking disappears into the framing before the tile goes on; lighting is layered for older eyes.
Designed beautifully, never clinically: you choose it for how it looks, and you keep it for how it lives.

One of ours is documented as a full case study — a Winter Springs primary bath planned for steam before a single tile went up. A Clermont primary bath took the zero-entry path instead — the dated shower rebuilt flush with the floor, the bulky corner tub squared off — in The Lakeside Blue. Prefer the wet-room path? Walk the full wet-room bathroom, where tub and shower share one glass-walled, fully waterproofed room.

■ THE STEAM SHOWER, DONE RIGHT · WINTER SPRINGS

CENTRAL FLORIDA REALITY

Permits, HOAs and older homes

BATHROOM RENOVATION HERE runs through Orange County or Seminole County permitting (or the City of Orlando / City of Winter Park when you're inside city limits) — plumbing, electrical and structural inspections included. We pull and manage the permits as the contractor of record; the inspections pass because the work behind the wall is right. You never stand in a permit line, and you never discover after the fact that your remodel happened off the books — a real problem when the house sells.

Windermere estate under an HOA or ARB (Isleworth, we know the drill)? We handle the submittal and the architectural review. 1950s College Park bungalow with cast-iron drains in the slab, or a 1980s Longwood ranch with a re-pipe in its future? We've opened those floors before and scope for it honestly instead of surprising you at demo.

Florida's building code is also why our waterproofing and ventilation details run past minimum: this climate punishes shortcuts with mold, and a luxury finish over a wet wall is not luxury.
The boring paperwork and the beautiful room are the same discipline.

Whole-Home Remodeling in Orlando — the design-build studio that renovates the entire house as one connected project.

Kitchens, baths, living spaces, and the walls between them — designed together, built together, by one team on one contract. This page walks you through one real house to show you why that matters.

THE HOUSE THIS PAGE WALKS THROUGH, ROOM TO ROOM — WHOLE-HOME REMODELING IN CELEBRATION

THE PREMISE

Most people call us about one room.

THE BEST HOMES COME from seeing all of them. Open the kitchen to the living room and the light changes in three other spaces. Move a wall and the primary suite gains a real bath. A whole-home remodel — a full-home renovation planned as one project — isn't a bigger invoice; it's a different way of thinking about the same house.

ONE DECISION CASCADES THROUGH THE FLOOR PLAN. That's why we'd rather design the whole house once than remodel it twice. And if your real question is even bigger — whether an older house is worth remodeling at all — start with our field note: Renovate or Rebuild? Deciding for an Older Central Florida Home.

A whole house remodel isn't about doing more rooms. It's about the connections between them — sightlines, light, and flow you can't get one room at a time.

ROOM TO ROOM · OCOEE

An Ocoee whole-home rebuild, walked in order

The family loved their street and had run out of room in the house. So the one-story home came down to its slab and two walls, then went back up with a raised ceiling, a second story, and a back yard built for living. Same street, new story.

01 · OCOEE · THE FRONT

Same lot, same slab, same neighbors. The one-story house that stood here is now two stories, and the street sees a new home where the old one stood.

02 · OCOEE · GREAT ROOM

The original ceiling was raised, and the great room now opens up under exposed wood beams. The kitchen, the dining area, and the new stair all share the same volume and the same light.

03 · OCOEE · KITCHEN

The kitchen opens straight onto the living area: a navy island with seating, white cabinetry to the ceiling, and a paneled hood on the cooking wall. One floor runs under all of it.

04 · OCOEE · STAIR + DINING

The new stair leads to the new second story: a guest bedroom with its own bath, an office, a powder bath, and a flex room set up for movies, separate so the sound doesn’t carry. Beneath it, built-in navy cabinetry and wine storage serve the dining table.

05 · OCOEE · THE BACK YARD

Across the back, a covered lanai with a built-in outdoor kitchen and a pool turned an open lawn into living space. Measured on the plans, living area grew from 2,462 to 3,709 square feet. Want the whole story? Read the Ocoee case study, or why we kept the slab in Keep the Slab, Keep the Street.

ROOM TO ROOM · WINTER PARK

A Winter Park whole-home renovation, walked in order

Every photo below is the same Winter Park house, photographed at completion. Watch how each room hands off to the next — that handoff is what you're actually buying.

01 · WINTER PARK · KITCHEN

The kitchen sets the house's material language: white oak, warm brass, quiet stone. But look at the edges of the frame — the room refuses to end at its own walls.

02 · WINTER PARK · KITCHEN + DINING + LIVING

One frame, three rooms. Dining, living, and kitchen share light, floor, and ceiling because the plan treated them as one space with three jobs — the whole-home argument in a single photograph.

03 · WINTER PARK · LIVING ROOM

From the sofa, the island is still in view. The fireplace wall and lit built-ins were designed against the kitchen elevation behind them — two rooms, one composition.

04 · WINTER PARK · PRIMARY BATH

Down the hall, the primary bath speaks the same language — the white oak and warm metals from the kitchen, translated into stone and water. That continuity is a whole-home decision; it can't be retrofitted one contractor at a time.

05 · WINTER PARK · THE CLOSE

The payoff of a connected plan is a house that feels finished everywhere you look — down to the last niche. Want the rest of this house? Walk the full Winter Park whole-home transformation.

ROOM TO ROOM · APOPKA

An Apopka whole-home remodel, walked in order

A 2014 builder-spec house that worked fine and still felt like somebody else’s. Beige tile, dark granite, and an aluminum slider gave way to one calm, connected main floor and a rebuilt primary suite. One design idea, carried through every room.

01 · APOPKA · KITCHEN

White cabinetry runs to the ceiling around one black island under three black pendants. That black returns, in small doses, in every room that follows. Past the island, French doors stand where the builder’s slider used to be.

02 · APOPKA · KITCHEN + LIVING

From the sofa, the kitchen reads as furniture. One continuous run of engineered hickory replaced the beige tile across the main level, so the floor never changes and the plan feels open even where no wall moved.

03 · APOPKA · LIVING ROOM

The French doors look like a finish selection. They are a structural change: the opening was cut wider into a concrete-block wall and carried on a new engineered header, permitted and inspected. Drapery and new lighting finish the room.

04 · APOPKA · LAUNDRY

The laundry was refit in the same language as the rooms guests see: open shelving, a warm wood counter over the machines, and a patterned tile floor underfoot.

05 · APOPKA · PRIMARY BATH

Down the hall, the primary bath finishes the thread: matte-black fittings, mirrors, and sconces over marble-veined quartz, with wood-look mosaic underfoot. Want the whole story, including the engineering behind those doors? Read the Apopka case study, or browse the full Apopka photo gallery.

THE WALL BETWEEN THE ROOMS

Bring us your load-bearing wall.

OPEN-CONCEPT PLANS USUALLY RUN THROUGH a wall that's holding the house up. That's not a reason to abandon the plan — it's a reason to hire a design-build firm with structural work in its everyday scope. Engineered beams, properly sized posts, rerouted plumbing and electrical: the unglamorous work that makes the connected floor plan possible, permitted, and inspected.

IT'S THE LANE AN INTERIOR-ONLY STUDIO CAN'T DRIVE IN. Our designers and builders plan the opening together — see how a KBF project runs, phase by phase. At the far end of that range, one Ocoee home was taken down to its slab and two walls and rebuilt with a second story: The Same Street, New Story.

Structural changes are always confirmed by field verification and, where required, a licensed structural engineer's design — we tell you what the wall needs before demolition, not after. What actually lives inside one of these walls — and what replacing it takes — is its own field note: What's Actually Behind a Load-Bearing Wall (and What Removing It Takes).

LIVING IN YOUR HOME WHILE WE REMODEL IT

Occupied-home honesty

MOST OF OUR WHOLE-HOME CLIENTS live in the house through construction. So the plan is built for it: work zoned in phases, dust containment at the zone boundaries, a functioning temporary kitchen when yours is down, and a weekly communication rhythm so you always know what's happening next week.

You'll also have eyes on the project between site visits — schedule, selections, and progress tracked in one place through our client portal, with your project manager a message away. The full six-phase structure is on the process page. And because open walls always know more than drawings do, we plan for what they'll reveal — the field note While the Walls Are Open: Planning for Scope You Can’t See Yet is that checklist in print.

■ ORLANDO · THE KITCHEN · REVIEWS × PROJECTS

ONE TEAM, ONE CONTRACT

The design studio that can also move the wall

THE COMMON ALTERNATIVE is a designer plus a general contractor plus a cabinet shop — three contracts, three schedules, and you as the general manager between them. KBF's model is design-build: the designer who draws your whole-home plan and the team that builds it work under one roof, with selections made in person at our Maitland showroom.

INTERIOR DESIGN ISN'T AN ADD-ON HERE — it's the front half of the same engagement. Our interior-design studio carries finishes, fixtures, and furnishings through the same plan, so the finished house reads as one hand's work.

THE RECORD

The company's project records now hold more than 1,000 completed projects across Central Florida — a derived count from 22 years of files — including 250+ Orlando projects over two decades — 88 of them verified in our records. DESIGN-BUILD HOME ADDITIONS

Home additions
Orlando, FL

FILMED: A COVERED-LIVING & SUMMER-KITCHEN ADDITION · ORLANDO · KBF PROJECT RECORDS, 2023

BOOK YOUR COMPLIMENTARY CONSULTATION
(407) 499-8694

4.8★ GOOGLE · 63 REVIEWS  ·  FL LICENSE CGC 1529022

Home Additions in Orlando — Design-Build Room Additions & Home Expansions Across Central Florida

A home addition here means permitted square footage added to your home — a primary suite, an in-law suite, a bonus room, or a great-room expansion. KBF Design Gallery designs, engineers, permits, and builds it as one design-build team from our Maitland studio — 1295 S. Orlando Ave., Maitland, FL 32751 — under Florida license CGC 1529022, so the architect, the engineering, and the crew that builds it never work from different assumptions.

A SECOND STORY & AN OUTDOOR-LIVING ADDITION

Built up and built out —
an Ocoee home, rebuilt on its slab

This one went well beyond a typical addition, and we’d rather say so plainly. In Ocoee, all but the slab and two walls of a one-story home came down. The original ceiling was raised, and a second story went on: a guest bedroom with its own bath, an office, a powder bath, and a flex room set up as a movie room. Across the back, a covered lanai, a built-in outdoor kitchen and a pool turned an open lawn into living space. Measured on the plans, living area grew from 2,462 to 3,709 square feet, and the back porch from 172 to 1,120.

The photographs follow the house in three stages: as we found it, during construction, and complete.

AS FOUND

AS FOUND · THE FRONT, FROM THE STREET
AS FOUND · THE BACK, AND AN OPEN LAWN

DURING CONSTRUCTION

THE SECOND STORY, FRAMED

WALK THE OCOEE PROJECT

Read why we kept the slab in Keep the Slab, Keep the Street, or watch the tour on YouTube. Every furnishing in the finished home was selected by the KBF Interior Design team — see it on the Interior Design page.

TWO WAYS TO BUY AN ADDITION

Shell-only,
or finished to the last cabinet pull

Every KBF addition starts with the same engineered structure. The difference is where our scope ends and yours begins. Use the tiers below as a general guide to what each includes — the scope of your project may vary.

BOTH TIERS INCLUDE: STRUCTURAL DESIGN BY A LICENSED ARCHITECT · ENGINEERING · HOA & MUNICIPALITY GUIDELINES DISCOVERY · SITE EVALUATION & PROPERTY SETBACKS · BEST ECONOMIC & CONSTRUCTION PLAN RECOMMENDATION · FINAL STAMPED DRAWINGS READY FOR PERMIT APPROVAL · PERMITS · PROJECT MANAGEMENT · SITE PREP · DEMO · FOUNDATION · FRAMING · INSULATION · DRYWALL · EXTERIOR STUCCO/SIDING · INTERIOR & EXTERIOR PAINT · INTERIOR & EXTERIOR DOORS · WINDOWS · WARRANTY
THE SHELL · THE SAME ORLANDO ADDITION PHOTOGRAPHED AT DRY-IN

TIER ONE

Shell-Only Addition

A blank canvas to create your own interior: the complete engineered structure, weathered-in and painted, ready for your own finish-out.

Mechanical, plumbing & electrical rough-ins
Dry-in roofing — shingles/tiles not included
THE FINISH · THE SAME ADDITION’S SUMMER KITCHEN, COMPLETED

TIER TWO

Full Addition with Interior Finishing

A fully finished interior, professionally designed by our interior designers and space planners — one contract from stamped drawings to styled shelves.

Full mechanical, plumbing & electrical
Dry-in roofing with shingles/tiles
Professionally designed interior architecture
Kitchen & bathroom design and space planning
Interior plans, 3-D renderings, storyboards & photo-realistic renderings
Cabinetry, lighting, hardware, plumbing fixtures, countertops, trim, flooring & bath tile — selection, product, and installation

WHICH TIER FITS IS USUALLY CLEAR within one conversation — it depends on whether you want one team through interior completion, or a sealed structure you finish your own way.

ONE ADDITION, ON THE RECORD

From open lawn to covered living —
one Orlando addition, start to finish

These are the client’s own photographs and our progress records of a single Orlando project — the covered-living and summer-kitchen addition in the film above — from the yard as we found it, through the engineered shell, to completion.

AS FOUND · THE ORIGINAL PATIO
AS FOUND · THE OPEN YARD
THE SHELL · MASONRY & ENGINEERED TRUSSES

COLONNADE BAYS & PAVER SURROUND

STONE, STEEL & WEATHERPROOF CABINETRY

Every project photograph on this page is a real KBF project. More finished work — including whole-home scopes with added square footage — lives in the Body of Work.

THE ADDITIONS WE BUILD

Adding permitted square footage,
one team under one contract

A home addition is structural work — a new foundation, a new roofline married to the old one, and every home system extended into space that didn't exist before. KBF designs, engineers, and builds it as one design-build team from the Maitland studio, under Florida license CGC 1529022.

Primary-Suite Additions

A new bedroom, bath, and closet volume added to the main level — a private suite gained without giving up the living space you already have.

In-Law & Multi-Generational Suites

Fully plumbed private suites with their own entry and living space, planned for long-term accessibility from the first drawing.

Bonus & Flex Rooms

Conditioned square footage over garages or into side yards — media rooms, offices, studios — engineered as real living space, not converted storage.

Great-Room & Kitchen Expansions

Pushing an exterior wall out to enlarge the heart of the house, usually paired with a load-bearing opening so the new space reads as one room.

Second-Story Additions

Building up when the lot can't build out — the heaviest structural lift we do, from foundation reinforcement to an entirely new roof system. See one in Ocoee, where a one-story home was rebuilt with a second story and a raised ceiling: The Same Street, New Story.

Not Sure It's an Addition?

If the space you need might already be inside your walls, a whole-home remodel can open it without adding footprint — we'll help you decide at the first consultation.

1,000+
PROJECTS ACROSS CENTRAL FLORIDA
88

A FAMILY & THEIR WHOLE-HOME SCOPE

“You helped me envision our dream and elevated it beyond what I could have imagined… It is airy, bright, minimal and provides a place we love coming home to. It is peaceful and calm… Our realtor told us that it's a one of a kind.”
THE MARCISZ FAMILY · APOPKA · KITCHEN, LIVING SPACES & PRIMARY SUITE · CLIENT TESTIMONIAL, VERBATIM

Their actual home — photographed on completion. When scope grows room to room, one team keeps it one project. More verified pairs live on the reviews page.

THE STRUCTURE BEHIND THE DRYWALL

Bring us your load-bearing wall

EVERY ADDITION LIVES OR DIES ON what you can't see at the walkthrough: the new foundation tied into the old one, the roof marriage that keeps water out for decades, the load path that carries the second story down to the ground, and the electrical, plumbing, and HVAC runs extended into the new space. We plan that structure first — before finishes, before fixtures — so the addition performs like it was always part of the house.

Every structural change is engineered and permitted; final structural design on every KBF project is produced by the licensed structural engineer of record.

WHETHER YOUR PROJECT SHOULD BE AN ADDITION at all is its own honest question — we wrote it down: Remodel or Add On? Reworking Space vs. Building New Square Footage.

CASE STUDY · WINTER PARK

A whole home,
opened and reworked

Walk the Winter Park transformation — structural openings, a reworked plan, and finished space the family lives in today. It's the closest look at how KBF handles walls that move and scope that grows.

WALK THE PROJECT

At KBF, we know the best way to learn about you, your style, and your goals for your home addition is to meet with you in person. In order for that consultation to be as beneficial to you as possible, we’ll need some important information about your existing home before we meet. Here’s the information we’ll discuss with you during our initial phone call: 

Which tier of addition are you interested in: a shell-only addition or full addition with interior finishing?

What is the purpose of the home addition: bedroom(s), bathroom(s), kitchen, office, game room, in-law suite, etc.?

IS THE ADDITION A FIRST-STORY ADDITION, a second-story addition to an existing second story, or adding an entirely new second-story to an existing one-story home?

How many square feet do you want to add to your home?

What is the age of your home’s roof?

Do you have your existing home’s blueprints/plans?

Do you have a recent survey of your property?

Do you know of existing setbacks for your home’s lot?

Is your home in an HOA? If so, are the bylaws for the HOA available?

Does your home have city sewer or a septic system? 

How long do you plan on staying in your home once the addition is complete?

What investment range are you considering for your home addition?

Based on our discussion and your wish list, we can provide a parameter of cost for our turnkey home addition services.

Frequently Asked Questions
How much does a home addition cost in Orlando?

Home addition investment depends on scope — a simple bonus room is a very different project from a second-story addition or a fully plumbed in-law suite that extends your foundation, roofline, and every home system. KBF begins by establishing a target investment together, then aligns the design, engineering, and construction scope to that target. After the in-home consultation and design development, you receive a fixed-scope written estimate before work begins. Any later change is documented and approved in writing before it affects cost or schedule.

Interior Design in Orlando & Central Florida — The Design Studio That Can Also Move the Wall

Full-service interior design and design-build remodeling under one roof — from concept and CAD through renderings, specifications, and installation — by the KBF Design Gallery team, family-owned in Maitland since 2003.

FEATURED PROJECT · OCOEE

A whole home in Ocoee, furnished by the KBF Interior Design team

OCOEE, FLORIDA · WHOLE-HOME REBUILD · 3,709 SQ FT OF LIVING AREA

The KBF design-to-build team kept this home’s slab and two of its walls, took the rest down, raised the original ceiling and added a second story. These are the finished rooms.

Every furnishing, decor piece, window treatment and piece of artwork in this home was selected by the KBF Interior Design team.

■ GREAT ROOM

The great room sits under the vaulted, beamed ceiling, with the kitchen, breakfast nook and dining area opening off it. A palette of navy, warm wood and soft blue-green runs through the house, from the kitchen island to the bedding and the bath drapes.

The structure, the before-and-afters and the walkthrough film are in the case study, The Same Street, New Story.

READ THE CASE STUDY

THE DIFFERENCE

Most designers hand your walls to someone else. We don't.

MOST INTERIOR DESIGNERS FINISH THE DRAWINGS, hand your walls to a separate contractor, and hope the two halves coordinate. KBF designs and builds. Selections from our Maitland showroom, structural changes, and installation live under one contract and one team — so a design decision that requires moving a wall becomes a drawing, not a renegotiation between two companies who've never met. We wrote the honest comparison down — Design-Build vs. Hiring a Designer and a Contractor Separately — including when two contracts serve you fine.

Design studios can't build. Design-build remodelers rarely design at this level. We do both — with an in-house interior-design team and our own construction crews, run on the same six-phase process every KBF project follows.

A wall in the way is not the end of the idea. It's the beginning of the engineering — and the reason this design studio keeps its builders in the same building.

■ WINTER PARK · FROM THE WHOLE-HOME REMODEL IN THE WHITE OAK RANCH

THE SCOPE, NAMED

Five phases. One team carries all of them.

EVERY FULL-SERVICE INTERIOR-DESIGN ENGAGEMENT moves through the same five phases — each one framed by the outcome it hands you, not a checklist of deliverables.

01
Concept

Spatial planning, mood, and the design direction for the whole home.

02
Detailing / CAD

Construction-ready drawings — where design meets the field, and where "move the wall" is engineered rather than improvised.

03
3D & Renderings

Photoreal views, so you approve the room before anything is built.

04
Specifications

Every finish, fixture, and material selected — many of them in person at the Maitland showroom.

05
Furnishings & Installation

Procurement, furniture, and the styled reveal — one team carries it to the last cushion.

■ APOPKA · THE TWO-TONE TRANSITIONAL

THE WALL IN THE WAY

When a wall carries the house, opening it is engineered work — a beam sized for the load, posts carrying it to the foundation, a permit issued against those exact drawings. See it real on our DeLand open-concept kitchen remodel, where two load-bearing walls came out under engineered structure.

Bring us your load-bearing wall.

THE BEST INTERIOR-DESIGN IDEA IN CENTRAL FLORIDA dies in the same place: at the wall between the kitchen and everything else. When that wall carries the house, a design-only studio has to stop drawing and start making phone calls. We keep drawing — because the engineered beam, the posts that carry the load to the foundation, and the plumbing and electrical rerouted out of that wall are our everyday scope, priced and sequenced inside the same plan as the cabinetry.

That's why this page lives under the KBF master brand and not a standalone studio: when the design wants the wall gone, the whole-home team is already on the project.

Structural changes are always confirmed by field verification and, where required, a licensed structural engineer's design — we tell you what the wall needs before demolition, not after.

Most studios design around the wall. We design through it — one contract, one team, one set of drawings that already knows what the beam costs.

THE PORTFOLIO, ON THE RECORD

Real rooms, photographed at completion

Every photograph below is a KBF interior-design project from our completion archive — no stock, no renders, no borrowed work.

01 · WINTER GARDEN · WHOLE-HOME INTERIOR DESIGN & REMODEL — LIGHT-FILLED LAKEFRONT PLAN, PLASTER AND PALE OAK

A whole home designed and remodeled as one composition: dining, living, and kitchen opened to the lake, a plaster hood banded in white oak, and a palette that lets the light do the finishing.

02 · BALDWIN PARK · LIVING ROOM INTERIOR DESIGN — FULL FURNISHINGS, BANQUETTE NOOK, CAPIZ AND LINEN

A furnishings-and-finishes project end to end: seating plan, banquette dining nook, lighting, textiles, and the styling — phase 05 as a finished fact.

03 · ORLANDO · TWO LIVING-ROOM PROJECTS — MID-CENTURY MODERN · DOWNTOWN FIREPLACE REBUILD

Two Orlando living rooms from the archive: a mid-century room composed around the clients' own furniture language, and a downtown fireplace rebuilt in black granite as the room's quiet anchor.

04 · GRANDE LAKES, ORLANDO · WHOLE-RESIDENCE INTERIOR DESIGN — TRAVERTINE, CHROME, AND FULL-HEIGHT LIGHT, STYLED TO THE LAST OBJECT

A full-residence design engagement at the Ritz-Carlton Residences at Grande Lakes — phase 05 across an entire home rather than one room: the living room composed around a travertine-and-oak fireplace wall, the primary suite built on a chrome canopy bed and upholstered paneling, every finish, furnishing, and object selected and placed by the studio, photographed at completion in 2022.

Outdoor living at KBF means the rooms outside your walls — summer kitchens, covered lanais, fireplace lounges, pergolas, and the terraces and pool surrounds that tie them together. KBF Design Gallery designs, engineers, permits, and builds them as one design-build team from our Maitland studio — 1295 S. Orlando Ave., Maitland, FL 32751 — under Florida license CGC 1529022, so the designer, the engineering, and the crew that builds it never work from different assumptions.

RESORT-STYLE COMFORT, AT HOME

Invest in your home and your life with unparalleled design and quality

At KBF Design Gallery, we create luxury outdoor living spaces that seamlessly blend sophisticated design with resort-style comfort. Whether you’re dreaming of a custom outdoor kitchen for entertaining, a tranquil fireplace lounge, or a full backyard transformation, our award-winning design-to-build team brings your vision to life with elegance and ease.

Experience the KBF Difference — where elevated design meets precision execution, and luxury is a given. Whether you’re ready for a full backyard renovation or looking to enhance your existing outdoor space, our team is here to bring your dreams to life.

THE WORK · I

One backyard, on the record — pool terrace, summer kitchen & fireplace lounge, Orlando

The film at the top of this page and the photographs below are the same Orlando project, from KBF’s project records: a raised glass-tile pool with submerged tables, a covered lounge with television and linear fireplace, and a stainless summer kitchen — one backyard designed as a single composition.

REVIEWS FROM OUR CLIENTS

In their own words
As we round the corner to finish up a few minor items, I just wanted to take the time to send a note of appreciation to your entire KBF team. I know I entered your showroom with skepticism and doubt after such a horrible experience with another local design firm. Your team was affirming, supportive, and lead the way in every way possible to make this next house project a success for our home. KBF has all my trust in quality workmanship. You all should be very proud of how you do your work. It is not common to find quality firms that do what they say they are going to do. Thank you for restoring my confidence.
— THE CARTERS
We want to express our satisfaction with our decision to go with KBF. We would like you to pass this on to all of your employees who participated on our job. What sets KBF apart from the competition is your ability to design, execute, and react quickly to any issues that come up along the way. You've put together an excellent team and we wish you continued success.
— THE DENHOFS
Working with KBF was a dream. KBF was able to take our dream and turn it into reality. Their team was extremely responsive and we truly feel like we gained new friends. Having never done any major home remodeling before, we were unsure what to expect, but were blown away by the professionalism of everyone KBF introduced us to. We finally have a house where we feel truly peaceful and where the home feels like it should have always been this way. We are beyond thankful for KBF and for them creating the home of our dreams.
— KELLY DIXON

BOOK A SIGNATURE CONSULT

Naming the anti-fit is the point: honest gating is what makes the certainty promise credible. If your project needs engineering, we tell you at the consult and route you to our Signature kitchens or Signature baths — see how a whole-home transformation actually gets decided. For the fit-gate in field-note form, read Same-Footprint vs. Full Remodel: Which Kitchen or Bath Renovation Do You Need?. And for what the design phase itself buys — and why it comes before any honest number — read What a Design Retainer Actually Buys You.

WHAT STUDIO KBF IS

Studio KBF is KBF Design Gallery's streamlined line for a designer-led, remove-and-replace transformation while keeping your existing layout — a kitchen, a primary bath, or every room in the house. The gate is complexity, not room count: if the layout stays, Studio KBF can take on any size of project, up to a whole-home remove-and-replace.

Every Studio project is delivered by the same award-winning team behind every KBF Design Gallery remodel — the same designers, the same project managers, the same 5-year craftsmanship warranty, working from the same Maitland showroom. What changes is the path: fewer decisions, a curated palette, and the same six-phase process on a constrained scope.

ONE RETAINER, RENDERED REAL

First the drawing. Then the room.
THE BUILT ROOM
THE STUDIO MODEL
DRAG TO COMPARE
◂▸

The Waterfall Kitchen · Winter Park. She had already worked with another designer — and retained Studio KBF to see what our creativity would do with the same room. The studio’s answer, modeled first and signed that September: take the glossy white kitchen and its bar-height seating wall out entirely, and set a marble-veined quartz island — “waterfall end on living room,” in the contract’s own words — inside the same footprint. Drag the line above: the studio’s model on the left, the photographed room on the right.

THE MODEL SETTLED THE ARCHITECTURE — THE ISLAND, THE TALL BANK, THE RUNS. THE MATERIAL STORY READS STRAIGHT OFF THE PROJECT’S OWN PAPERWORK: RECONSTITUTED-WALNUT SLAB FRONTS, QUARTZ, WARM BRASS.

COMPLETION
CONSULT DAY
◂▸

THE BEFORE IS HER CONSULT-DAY PHONE SNAPSHOT — SHOWN AT ITS TRUE SIZE, NEVER ENLARGED.

The consult sheet asked. The room answered.
“ALL NEW”
The contract took out the cabinets, counters, backsplash, appliances — and the wooden seating area.
“OPEN TO INDUCTION”
The gas range left with the old kitchen. A 36-inch Thermador induction cooktop and a single electric wall oven took the run.
“INTEGRATED FRIDGE”
A Thermador built-in, paneled into the tall bank behind one long brass pull.
“WINE FRIDGE”
Wired into the plan — the wine refrigerator gets its own outlet in the contract’s electrical scope.
“DRAWERS”
Drawer stacks across the perimeter, with pop-up outlets in the island so the quartz stays uninterrupted.
“TV WALL — NEEDS STORAGE”
The entertainment wall shipped in the same contract as the kitchen: one hand, one contract, both rooms.
The refrigerator the consult sheet asked for — there, and invisible.
Induction where the gas range stood, under a stacked-mosaic splash.
The powder bath joined by change order — new vanity, new mirror, quilted wallpaper; the existing sink and top reset in place. The studio spends where it shows.

That is what a retainer buys: the drawing, the decisions, and the room that matches both. What a Design Retainer Actually Buys →

WHY IT FEELS CERTAIN

Speed is the result of a constrained scope — not a countdown.
ONE CURATED PALETTE · RESOLVED BEFORE YOU ARE ASKED TO CHOOSE
Fewer decisions

A curated palette instead of an open showroom. Your designer has already resolved the hard combinations; your selection session tailors, it doesn't start over.

No structural unknowns

Because the layout stays, there are no load-bearing surprises and no engineered-beam change orders mid-build. What we scope is what we build.

One plan set

A streamlined plan set — layout, elevations, finishes — with standard electrical and plumbing permitting handled by KBF as the licensed contractor of record.

One team, one contract, one warranty

One dedicated project manager, the KBF install team, and the same 5-year craftsmanship warranty that covers every KBF remodel.

SAME FOOTPRINT, PROVEN

The room stayed exactly where it was. Everything in it changed.

The black-and-white checkerboard floor — kept. It is in both photographs.
2
The fluted casing and its bull’s-eye corner block — the house’s original trim, painted rather than replaced. Visible here in the after frame.

A laundry room in Winter Springs — and the clearest picture of what a same-footprint remodel actually is. The checkerboard floor stayed. The house’s fluted door casings and their bull’s-eye corner blocks were kept and painted rather than replaced — one of them, olive, is marked in the after frame. What changed is everything you touch: deep-olive cabinetry carried up to a crown, a quartz counter and base cabinets where there were none, brass hardware, a new washer and dryer. Keep what the house already gives you; replace everything that shows.

Both photographs are the same room, taken from the doorway — the before looking in, the after standing just inside — so they are not the same angle, and nothing here pretends they are. The one thing you can check across both frames is marked ① on each: the floor. The casing detail, ②, is in the after frame only. The blurred patch on the wall of the before is a family photograph, hidden at the owners’ expense of a tidy picture rather than theirs. More from this project — remodeling in Winter Springs →

And what it costs

We don’t publish a Studio KBF price, and we won’t invent one over the phone — not because it is a secret, but because the honest number rests on two things nobody has seen yet: how much of the house you are touching, and the level of finish you choose. The same laundry can be built three different ways.

What is fixed is the path to the number. Your complimentary consultation confirms the project fits Studio KBF. The designer-led selection session sets the palette. The price is then built with you against real selections, line by line, before you commit to a build. And if the project turns out to need a wall moved, we say so at the consult and route you to KBF Signature rather than quietly pricing it as something it is not.
